description.narrative: Building on a series of analytical engagements, technical assistance (TA) and support for sectoral reforms delivered by the World Bank (WB) over the past seven years in the digital domain as well as deep engagement and investment operations in the health sector in Senegal, the proposed project is designed to help the Government of Senegal (GoS) accelerate its digital transformation and digital inclusion, including in healthcare provision. The Project is articulated around four key, integrated and mutually reinforcing components at the policy, infrastructure, and services levels, jointly contributing to green, resilient and inclusive development (GRID) in Senegal. These components seek to (i) enhance an enabling climate-informed legal, regulatory, and institutional environment for the digital economy; (ii) expand resilient broadband infrastructure with a focus on the national fiber optic backbone and last-mile connectivity in lagging zones of Casamance and Groundnut Basin; (iii) support digital transformation of the public sector by strengthening e-government technical foundations and services and digital adoption through improved digital literacy and skills, particularly of women and youth; and (iv) drive the development and uptake of selected digital health systems and services. The project also includes project management component and a Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) that would allow for a quick disbursement of any uncommitted balances as a swift response to eligible crises or emergencies that could arise during project implementation. The first component will finance several TA packages to strengthen legal and regulatory “analog foundations”, underpinning a safe and inclusive digital economy. It will focus on laws and regulations that foster the emergence of a digital economy as well as the capacity of senior government officials tasked with designing, implementing and evaluating these. The measures will be aimed at (i) increasing broadband competition (including through support to commercializing fiber optic assets of the national holding company SENUM) and hence improving affordability of broadband services; (ii) strengthening the telecom market regulation (including on key aspects related to climate change impact of the digital sector, infrastructure sharing, spectrum management, digital financial services (DFS) and USSD); (iii) updating and implementing telecom and digital legislation (pertaining to electronic communications and information society laws and decrees, including data protection and cybersecurity, as well as a legal and regulatory framework for interoperability between public administrations); (iv) supporting a digital economy observatory by financing two waves of biennial national household and enterprises surveys on the availability and quality of digital infrastructure and the usage of digital services across the country (gender-disaggregated). The second component will finance TA and construction works to expand digital connectivity and henceforth digital inclusion across the country. In support of Maximizing Finance for Development (MFD) principles when expanding digital connectivity, public financing will only be employed to the extent necessary to reach areas, where private sector interest is insufficient to provide connectivity without public intervention or incentives. The project will finance both a package of TA activities as well as the actual construction of the priority missing links of the fiber optic national backbone under a PPP arrangement model. The project will also finance necessary feasibility studies as well as the construction of the missing access (last-mile) infrastructure with a specific focus to improve and expand coverage of underserved/uncovered villages in Casamance and the Groundnut Basin regions, which have a high level of poverty incidence and are lagging behind other parts of the country in terms of access to digital services.The third component will seek to boost digital adoption, focusing on developing useful content through digital public services and strengthening digital skills of the population. More specifically, the component will will finance TA activities as well as hardware and software to put in place technical foundations of e-government (including interoperability and government ente rprise architecture) and improve access and quality of citizen-centric digital public services (with an initial focus on selected use cases). Moreover, it will finance activities aimed at improving digital literacy and digital skills of people in targeted regions (aligned with those covered by Component 2 to maximize synergies), with a specific focus on youth and women, to drive the usage of digital technologies and associated value-added services and thus improve inclusion, productivity, and employability of the population. The fourth component will support the Ministry of Health and Social Action (MSAS) in the digitalization of selected health systems and services, contributing to the implementation of the Digital Health Strategic Plan 2018-2023 (Plan Strategique Sante Digitale, PSSD). More specifically, activities under this component will support critical pre-requisites for a successful digital health roll-out, including electronic medical records (EMR) – improved connectivity, data infrastructure, and equipment of health facilities; stronger health sector governance and coordination mechanisms; enabling legal and regulatory frameworks specific to healthcare services (in full alignment with legal and regulatory framework for broader digital economy to be supported under Component 1); and enhanced capacity at all levels of the healthcare pyramid through continuous trainings and change management. Building on these foundational pre-requisites, the component will also support setting up a digital health ecosystem to enable the deployment of secure health information systems (upgrading existing ones and developing new) based on coherent governance and interoperability framework. These systems will inter alia target the dematerialization of the patient journey, the empowerment of patients through increased access to high-quality and secure health information and the initiation of telemedicine services. The proposed project, will also include two standard components: (i) support to project management; and (ii) CERC that would allow for quick disbursements of any uncommitted balances as a swift response to eligible crises or emergencies that could arise during project implementation.The proposed project is fully aligned with the FY20–FY24 World Bank Group (WBG) Country Partnership Framework (CPF) for Senegal, having strong direct synergies with its three pillars. The CPF aims to support the vision of Senegal as an equitable middle-income economy by 2035, relying on three main pillars: (i) building human capital to enhance productivity and ignite the demographic dividend, including by promoting youth employability as well as health of various population groups, especially women and children; (ii) boosting competitiveness and job creation through private sector led growth, including by improving digital connectivity; and (iii) increasing resilience and sustainability in the context of growing risks, including by improving government's effectiveness, efficiency and transparency. The proposed project is directly linked to and highly synergetic with all the three pillars, as it aims to help the GoS (i) strengthen an enabling legal, regulatory and institutional environment for the digital economy and, thereby, level the playing field for private sector investments (in support of CPF Pillar 2); (ii) expand access to affordable high-quality broadband connectivity (in support of CPF Pillar 2, Objective 2.1); (iii) support digital adoption by strengthening digital skills of the population, with a focus on women and youth to make them more competitive in the labor market (in sup

condition.narrative: Hire one environmental and social specialist, in each PIU no later than three (3) months after the Project Effective Date, andthereafter maintain these positions throughout project implementation, as specified in the ESCP.

The Recipient shall exchange views with the Association on each such proposed consolidated annual work plan and budget and takeinto account comments which the Association may have before finalizing its annual work plan and budget not later than one (1) monthafter the date of its submission (Section I.C.3 of Schedule 2 to the FA).

The Recipient shall prepare and adopt, no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, and thereafter maintain, throughoutthe period of implementation of the Project, a manual (the “Project Operation Manual” or “POM”) in form and substance acceptable tothe Association (Section I.B.1 of Schedule 2 to the FA).

The Recipient shall, no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date for the Fiscal Year in which this Agreement shall becomeeffective, and September 1st of each subsequent Fiscal Year, furnish to the Association for the Association's no objection, aconsolidated annual program of activities proposed for implementation under the Project during the following Fiscal Year, togetherwith a proposed budget incorporating all funds which are or may become available to the Project (Section I.C.1 of Schedule 2 to theFA).

The Recipient shall, no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, establish and thereafter maintain a steering committeefor the Project with terms of reference, composition, and resources acceptable to the Association (Section I.A.2(a) of Schedule 2to the FA).

The Recipient shall, no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, or such other date which the Association has confirmedin writing to the Recipient is acceptable for the Project, establish under the leadership of its minister responsible for digitaleconomy and thereafter maintain, a team of experts collectively referred to as a unit (the “MCTEN Project Implementation Unit” or“MCTEN PIU”), with terms of reference, composition, and resources acceptable to the Association, and shall maintain these positionsfilled throughout the period of implementation of the Project (Section I.A.3(b)(i) of Schedule 2 to the FA).

The Recipient shall, no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, or such other date which the Association has confirmedin writing to the Recipient is acceptable for the Project, establish under the leadership of its minister responsible for healthand thereafter maintain, a team of experts collectively referred to as a unit (the “MSAS Project Implementation Unit” or “MSASPIU”), with terms of reference, composition and resources acceptable to the Association, and shall maintain these positions filledthroughout the period of implementation of the Project (Section I.A.3(c)(i) of Schedule 2 to the FA).

The Recipient shall, no later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, establish and thereafter maintain and operatethroughout the period of implementation of the project a grievance mechanism, as specified in the Environmental and SocialCommitment Plan (ESCP).
